topic: The Determinant: The Magic Scaling Factor
target_audience: University students (Introductory Linear Algebra) or Advanced High School students

sections.title: The Hook: The Morphing Canvas
lecture_lines: Imagine Pixel the Cat sitting on a unit grid.
A matrix transformation tilts and stretches the entire space.
Pixel’s shape changes, becoming taller, thinner, or slanted.
The determinant measures the change in Pixel’s total area.
It is the scaling factor for every shape in space.
animations: Initialize a #FFFFFF unit square grid; place a white character 'Pixel' at (0.5, 0.5).
Animate the grid and 'Pixel' morphing via matrix [[2, 1], [0.5, 1.5]].
The unit square becomes a parallelogram; 'Pixel' stretches accordingly.
Fill the transformed unit square area with #FFFF00 at 0.3 opacity.
Create a pulsing '?' text over the transformed area.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Basis vectors i-hat and j-hat define the unit square.
The matrix tells us where these vectors land.
Their new positions determine the transformation's resulting area.
animations: Draw red (#FF0000) vector (1,0) and green (#00FF00) vector (0,1) from origin.
Draw a white (#FFFFFF) dashed square with corners (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1).
Transform vectors to (3,0) and (0,2); expand square to 3x2 rectangle.

sections.title: Defining the Determinant Geometrically
lecture_lines: This unit square represents a starting area of one.
The transformation reshapes the square into a parallelogram.
Observe the area has now scaled to six.
This scaling factor applies to every shape in space.
The determinant represents this magic area scaling factor.
animations: Highlight a unit square [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] area and label it 'Area = 1'.
Transform the square [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] into a parallelogram using matrix [[3, 1], [0, 2]].
Animate the label 'Area = 1' changing into 'Area = 6' (#FFFF00).
Draw a circle [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circle.svg]; transform it into an ellipse using the same matrix.
Display text 'Determinant = 6' at the top of the screen in #FFFF00.

sections.title: The Calculation: The 2x2 Formula
lecture_lines: A 2x2 matrix defines the transformation’s movement.
The formula ad minus bc computes the scaling factor.
Calculating our example results in a determinant of six.
animations: Display matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] next to the parallelogram.
Show formula 'ad - bc' in #00FFFF; highlight 'ad' and 'bc' components.
Replace variables with 3, 1, 0, 2 and animate the result to 6.

sections.title: The Sign: Negative Determinants & Orientation
lecture_lines: Start with Pixel and our standard basis vectors.
A negative determinant mirrors Pixel to the other side.
Notice i-hat and j-hat have swapped their relative orientation.
This swap means we have flipped the entire space.
A negative sign indicates this fundamental change in orientation.
animations: Show 'Pixel' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] (#FFFFFF) facing right; label basis vectors i (red) and j (green).
Apply matrix [[-1, 0], [0, 1]]; 'Pixel' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] mirrors to face left.
Highlight that i is now to the left of j (flipped orientation).
Animate a circular arrow showing orientation direction reversing.
Display 'Negative Determinant = Flip' in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Zero Case: Collapsing Dimensions
lecture_lines: Some transformations land both basis vectors on one line.
This collapses the entire plane, losing all area.
A zero determinant means the transformation is not invertible.
animations: Start with standard grid; animate i and j moving to (1,1).
Shrink all grid lines until they align perfectly on the line y = x.
Fade in red (#FF0000) text 'Area = 0' and 'Not Invertible'.

sections.title: Summary & Real-world Intuition
lecture_lines: Determinants scale, flip, or collapse our mathematical world.
Graphics engines use them to render shadows and reflections.
It is the fundamental scaling factor of linear algebra.
animations: Display three small grids side-by-side: scaled, flipped, and collapsed, enhanced with [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shadows.svg] for depth.
Label them 'Det > 0', 'Det < 0', and 'Det = 0' respectively, alongside [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ref.svg] to indicate the transformation reference.
Morph all labels into 'The Magic Scaling Factor' in large yellow (#FFFF00) text.
